title: malbsMd: "I actually had an offer for Tier 1 VALORANT"
SkewMond envoyé en LCS ?
content:
L’avenir de Rudy « SkewMond » Semaan continue d’agiter le mercato de League of Legends. Alors que Sheep Esports révélait récemment que le Français ne ferait plus partie du cinq de départ de G2 Esports en 2027, de nouvelles informations viennent éclairer les intentions de l’organisation européenne. Selon le média espagnol Esportmaniacos , G2 aurait déjà pris contact avec une équipe nord-américaine pour négocier le transfert de son jungler. Et pas n’importe laquelle, puisqu’il s’agirait de Shopify Rebellion, une structure réputée pour disposer de moyens financiers importants.

Mais les discussions auraient rapidement buté sur les exigences de G2. Toujours selon la même source, Shopify Rebellion aurait jugé le montant demandé pour le rachat du contrat de SkewMond tout simplement trop élevé. « G2 aurait déjà essayé de le vendre à une équipe nord-américaine, mais cette équipe aurait répondu que, pour le moment, le montant réclamé était inabordable » , explique le média espagnol. Aucun chiffre précis n’a toutefois été communiqué. Sous contrat jusqu’en novembre 2028, le joueur de 22 ans représente encore un actif important pour G2, qui ne souhaiterait pas le laisser partir gratuitement.

Cette situation a de quoi surprendre au regard des performances de SkewMond cette saison. Le jungler français a été l’un des grands artisans de la domination de G2 en Europe, avec trois titres remportés en LEC et une distinction de MVP de la finale du Spring Split. Il s’était également illustré lors du First Stand, contribuant au parcours des Samouraïs jusqu’en finale. Mais l’élimination prématurée de G2 aux Worlds 2026 semble avoir précipité une reconstruction de l’effectif. L’organisation aurait ainsi décidé de miser sur Lyncas, en provenance de Vitality, pour occuper la jungle en 2027.

Reste désormais à savoir où SkewMond poursuivra sa carrière. Si la piste Shopify Rebellion semble compliquée financièrement à ce stade, elle témoigne de l’intérêt que pourrait susciter le Français outre-Atlantique. Plusieurs équipes européennes pourraient également chercher à renforcer leur roster pendant l’intersaison, même si le montant exigé par G2 risque de constituer un obstacle majeur. Affaire à suivre…

title: What are Kill Modes in Modern Warfare 4? Answered
content:
There are dozens of different challenges available to complete in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. From weapon Mastery Camos to daily challenges to Prestige challenges, there’s always something for you to be working towards in multiplayer and DMZ. However, if you opt to try and go for some of the calling card challenges in Modern Warfare 4, you’ll need to know what Kill Modes are.

You’re required to play “Kill Modes” for a variety of different calling card challenges in MW4, so here’s what they are and how to play them.

Fortunately, there’s a very simple explanation for what Kill Modes are in MW4. Plain and simple, they are game modes where the sole objective is to kill the enemy team. Any game mode with a side objective, such as collecting dog tags in Kill Confirmed, cash in Inflation, or capturing flags in Domination, isn’t considered a Kill Mode since score isn’t determined by kills alone.

As you might expect by now, there aren’t too many confirmed Kill Modes in MW4. However, the two Kill Modes are hugely popular, and they’re Team Deathmatch and Free-For-All . Playing either TDM or FFA in MW4 counts as playing a Kill Mode, so these modes will progress any challenge that requires that specific mode in multiplayer.

We recommend playing Team Deathmatch for most Kill Mode challenges, as you have easier opportunities to kill enemy players and there’s a team around you to help out with scorestreaks. However, if you want the most chances possible to kill enemies, then Free-For-All is the way to go, as no teammate can steal your potential kills.

In any case, you now have a guaranteed way to get kills while playing Kill Modes in Modern Warfare 4. With that out of the way, you can move on to completing other challenges, such as getting Longshot Kills or Point Blank Kills .

title: How to get Point Blank Kills in Modern Warfare 4
content:
There are some weapon camo challenges throughout Call of Duty history that give players the most trouble. In Modern Warfare 4 , several of these camo challenges have returned, including getting Point Blank Kills. These types of kills have long been a thorn in the side of camo grinders, but there are ways to make getting Point Blanks much easier in multiplayer.

Below, we’ll go through how to get Point Blank Kills and the best ways to go about doing so in Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer.

For starters, a Point Blank Kill is earned when you eliminate an enemy that is in extremely close proximity to you. It doesn’t matter when you damage an enemy, but when you see the kill pop up in the killfeed, you need to be within a certain range of the enemy for it to count as a Point Blank.

The exact range for a Point Blank Kill in Modern Warfare 4 is currently unknown, but we do know that it’s much closer than you might expect. In most cases, you need to be within roughly two meters of an enemy when you kill them to earn a Point Blank. This goes for all weapon classes as well, so unlike Longshot Kills , you have to be roughly two meters away even if you’re using something like a light machine gun or sniper rifle.

Now that you understand what a Point Blank Kill is, what’s the most optimal way to go about earning them in multiplayer? Well, it slightly depends on the gun you’re using, as some weapons are naturally stronger at closer ranges.

However, for the most part, you’ll want to use mobility attachments on your loadout so you can get your gun up quicker, which helps out tremendously when killing enemies at close-range. You could also go for an entirely hip-fire build and just shoot from the hip when killing enemies up close. This works best for most weapons, but you can ADS with something like an SMG or assault rifle and have the same results.

title: YouTube Is Reportedly Hosting a GTA 6 Creator Collective in London Before Launch
content:
YouTube is reportedly hosting a special Creator Collective event for GTA 6 in West London on November 17, two days before the game launches. Neither YouTube nor Rockstar Games has announced the event publicly, and no guest list has been shared.

If the report is accurate, it would be one of the clearest signs yet of how much the biggest video platform expects to gain from GTA 6. The game releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and the first few days after launch are likely to be among the busiest in YouTube gaming history.

Creator Collectives are in-person events that YouTube runs for people who make videos on the platform. According to the official YouTube Blog , they are “designed by creators, for creators” and are meant to help channels build community, expand their reach and grow their businesses. YouTube has held them around the world since 2022, and in 2025 it took them to all 50 US states to mark the platform’s 20th anniversary.

Most Creator Collectives are general meetups for creators at every stage. A session built around a single game would be unusual, and that is what makes this one stand out.

Details are thin. The reports so far give a date, November 17, and a location, West London. They do not say which creators are invited, whether Rockstar is involved, or whether anyone will get to play the game early.

That last point is the one fans will care about most. Rockstar has kept a tight grip on GTA 6 ahead of launch, and rumours of early access have already caused a stir. We looked at one of them in our piece on whether Shirrako has GTA 6 early . Until YouTube or Rockstar says otherwise, there is nothing to suggest this event includes hands-on time.

title: Nintendo Says It Is Not Considering Another Switch 2 Price Rise
content:
Nintendo says it is not planning another Switch 2 price rise. In its latest earnings presentation, released on November 5, the company said it has enough consoles in stock that it does not need to raise the price any time soon, even as memory shortages push hardware costs up across the industry.

That matters because the Switch 2 has already gone up once. Nintendo raised the US price from $450 to $500 in May, citing memory costs and US tariffs, and made similar increases in other regions. For anyone waiting on a holiday purchase, the message from Kyoto is that today’s price should hold.

Nintendo addressed the question head-on in its earnings materials, as first reported by VGC. The company acknowledged the industry-wide shortage of memory chips, which has driven up the cost of building consoles, phones and PCs this year. However, it said its current stock of Switch 2 units means it is not considering another increase.

Nintendo did not say how long that stock will last, or what it would do if the shortage drags on. That is the part to watch. A memory maker has already warned that supply will stay tight into 2027, so this is a promise about the near term, not a price freeze.

Back in May, Nintendo told investors it expected about 100 billion yen in extra costs over the financial year, driven by “rising component prices, particularly for memory, and tariff measures.” The US price rise followed soon after.

Nintendo is far from alone. Sony and Microsoft have both raised hardware prices this generation, and every current console now costs more than it did at launch. That includes the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, which came out six years ago. For a long time, consoles got cheaper as they got older. This generation has flipped that pattern.

title: LFL : Skeanz vers Galions, mais un retour en LEC reste possible
content:
Le mercato continue de s’agiter sur la scène française de League of Legends. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Duncan « Skeanz » Marquet aurait trouvé un accord verbal avec Galions pour la saison 2027. Le jungler de SK Gaming devrait ainsi retrouver la LFL, un championnat qu’il connaît bien après ses passages chez Vitality.Bee et la Karmine Corp. Mais rien n’est encore totalement acté : l’accord comprendrait une clause lui permettant de privilégier une offre du LEC si une équipe de l’élite européenne venait à se manifester durant l’intersaison. Dans le cas contraire, Skeanz devrait officiellement s’engager avec Galions à l’ouverture du marché des transferts.

Ce retour en France pourrait permettre au joueur de relancer sa carrière après une année particulièrement difficile. Recruté par SK Gaming dans le cadre d’un projet ambitieux, aux côtés de joueurs expérimentés comme Wunder et Mikyx, Skeanz n’a jamais véritablement réussi à s’imposer en LEC. La structure allemande a traversé une saison 2026 catastrophique, manquant les playoffs lors des trois splits. Même le remplacement de LIDER par SlowQ durant l’été n’a pas permis d’inverser la tendance. Malgré quelques performances encourageantes, le Français n’est pas parvenu à retrouver la régularité qui avait fait sa réputation sur la scène nationale.

Pour Galions, l’arrivée potentielle de Skeanz constituerait un renfort d’expérience après une saison historique. La structure française a dominé la scène européenne secondaire en remportant les EMEA Masters du Spring et du Summer Split, confirmant son statut de référence parmi les équipes des ligues régionales. Sa rivalité avec Solary a également marqué l’année 2026, les deux formations se disputant régulièrement les principaux titres. Avec un tel palmarès, Galions abordera forcément la prochaine saison avec de grandes ambitions.

Le recrutement de Skeanz pourrait également s’accompagner d’un autre retour important. Toujours selon Sheep Esports , le midlaner Tolga « Serin » Ölmez devrait lui aussi retrouver Galions en 2027. Les deux joueurs formeraient ainsi un duo mid-jungle expérimenté, capable de maintenir l’équipe parmi les meilleures formations de LFL. Reste toutefois une inconnue majeure : l’avenir de Skeanz dépendra des opportunités qui pourraient s’ouvrir en LEC dans les prochaines semaines. Si aucune offre ne se concrétise, Galions pourrait réaliser l’un des recrutements les plus intéressants du mercato français.

title: GTA 6 Pre-Orders Are Closing In on Cyberpunk 2077: How the 7.7 Million Estimate Stacks Up
content:
GTA 6 has not even launched, and it is already in record territory. Data firm Sensor Tower estimates the game has passed 7.71 million pre-orders, worth about $751 million, with roughly two weeks to go before release.

That number on its own is hard to picture. So we lined it up against two other huge launches, Cyberpunk 2077 and GTA 5, to see where it actually stands.

About 7.71 million, according to Sensor Tower’s estimate. These are not official figures. Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive have not shared any pre-order numbers, so this is a data firm’s model of the market, and it may not fully account for cancellations.

We have been following the numbers from the start on our GTA 6 pre-orders tracker , and our earlier report covers when pre-orders first passed $750 million .

Cyberpunk 2077 is the usual benchmark for pre-orders. CD Projekt said the game had about 8 million pre-orders before its December 2020 launch. GTA 6 sits just under 300,000 short of that, with two weeks of sales still to come. Unless something unusual happens, it should pass Cyberpunk before launch day.

There is a key difference. Cyberpunk launched on PC as well as consoles. GTA 6 is console-only for now, which makes its number even more striking.

title: Is the Free Fire India APK Safe? The Official Way to Download the Game
content:
Free Fire India is finally here, and so are the fake download links. Since Garena launched the game in India on October 28, searches for a “Free Fire India APK” have been everywhere. Before you tap on one, there is a simpler and safer route.

Free Fire India is available on the Google Play Store and the Apple App Store. You do not need an APK file from a third-party site to play it.

Not from an unknown website. Garena has not named any official APK download site for Free Fire India, so any APK you find online comes from a third party. Those files can be modified versions of the game, can carry malware, or can ask for permissions that a game has no reason to need.

There is also your account to think about. A fake build that asks you to log in can steal your Google, Facebook or game login. If something goes wrong, there is no official support for an app you installed from outside the store.

Open the Google Play Store, search for Free Fire India, and check that the developer is listed as Garena. Tap Install, wait for the download to finish, then open the game and log in. Updates arrive through the Play Store, so you never have to hunt for a new file.

Open the App Store, search for Free Fire India, and confirm the publisher is Garena. Tap Get, then open the game once it installs. iPhones do not support APK files at all, so any site promising an iOS APK is not genuine.

title: G2 cut ties with Perkz hours after his viral statement on faith and abortion
content:
G2 Esports have ended their relationship with Luka “Perkz” Perković, terminating the head coach of their League of Legends team less than 14 hours after he posted a long personal statement on X. In a statement signed by CEO Alban Dechelotte on 5 November, G2 said some of the views shared “do not align with G2’s stance and values”, and apologised to fans who had been hurt by them.

The decision brings an abrupt end to a second spell that began only in July and included a record 20th LEC title.

G2’s statement does not name Perkz, although it refers to a statement shared “by the Head Coach of one of our teams” the night before, which matches his post. “G2 is a diverse and international organization with different people from all around the world,” it reads, adding that respecting that diversity is “of the utmost importance” when representing the club.It closes by saying G2 will now rebuild its staff and roster, but “will not be able to communicate any changes until free agency officially opens.”

Perkz opened his post shortly after midnight UTC, explaining that he had been “very distant from social media and public touch for many years”. This, he said, would be his “first and last honest post in last decade”. He said he wanted to answer what he called “insanely fake narratives” about him as a person, rather than as a player. “I’m writing it so that at the very least you can hate me for what I really stand for,” he wrote.

The first of those narratives concerned Andrew Tate. Perkz said the claims grew out of him liking “a few tate memes” around 2022, when likes were still visible on Twitter, and he was blunt about where he stands. “I don’t like, support, or stand with tates,” he wrote, adding that he dislikes their views on life and their “wrongful teachings to younglings about women”.

He also defended his past support for G2 founder Carlos Rodriguez, who stepped down as CEO in 2022 after backlash over a video of him partying with Tate. Perkz described Rodriguez as “a good mentor to me”, someone who believed in him as a teenager when few others did. Even so, he criticised how Rodriguez handled his exit from G2, and he said the pair have since gone completely different ways.

title: Hades Says ‘I’m Guilty’ as Team Apex Gaming Link Reopens Unpaid Loans Row
content:
Hades, the former GodLike Esports figure who was accused last December of collecting money from people in the Indian gaming community and failing to repay it, has now admitted on X that he is “guilty”. His response came on 5 November, only hours after the community page letsgrowesports claimed that he had been working behind the scenes at Team Apex Gaming since Jonathan founded the organisation. Hades denied being formally part of TAG, but he also confirmed that he has already worked on “few projects” with it.

The row began on the night of 4 November, during Jonathan’s 8 Million Special stream on YouTube. Several guests at the Halloween-themed celebration wore masks, and community pages claimed that one masked guest who never revealed his face was Hades, pointing to a tattoo on his hand that stayed visible on camera. Hades has not said directly whether he was that guest, although his replies the next morning confirmed that he has been working with TAG in some capacity.

Okay so this scammer aka Hades is now a part of Team Apex Gaming Management? He was seen on Jonathan's stream yesterday hiding himself behind a mask without unveiling himself even though when others did… https://t.co/oLfh70ejv6

Hades’s first move was to go after letsgrowesports itself, questioning the page’s motives and challenging its admin to a one-on-one podcast. Soon afterwards, he turned to the question most fans were asking. “Regarding my role in TAG or anything around it, don’t make any assumptions,” he wrote, before adding that he is “not part of them yet” and is “just seeing if things will work out or no”. In the same post, he said he had “done few projects with them already”, without explaining what those projects involved.

Regarding my role in TAG or anything around it , don't make any assumptions, I'm not part of them yet and just seeing if things will work out or no , have done few projects with them already. I'm on my own path figuring things now , time will tell everything Peace out

On the money itself, Hades did not deny borrowing it. Replying to a fan, he said he had borrowed money, asked for more time and was unable to pay on time, before moving to a new country and working there to clear “few people”. “I’m not saying I’m victim here, I’m guilty but the numbers and facts people share is fake,” he added, while insisting that it is “not a scam if you return it”.

title: LFL : Boukada chez Solary, Zicssi arrive en LEC ?
content:
Solary tient peut-être déjà son premier renfort pour la saison prochaine. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , Mehdi « Boukada » Lahlou aurait trouvé un accord verbal avec la structure française pour rejoindre son équipe League of Legends en 2027. Toujours sous contrat avec Shifters, le jungler de 22 ans devrait officiellement s’engager après le 16 novembre. Il viendrait remplacer Lanzo « Zicssi » Ciajolo, l’un des grands artisans des succès de Solary cette année, qui pourrait quant à lui découvrir l’élite européenne. Le jeune Français serait notamment en discussions avancées avec SK Gaming, même si aucun accord définitif n’a encore été trouvé.

Pour Boukada, ce transfert marquerait un retour en LFL après une expérience contrastée en LEC. Révélé sur la scène française, il avait rejoint SK Gaming début 2025 avant d’attirer l’attention de BDS, devenue Shifters, qui avait déboursé près de 200 000 euros pour le recruter. Malgré quelques performances encourageantes, le Français n’est jamais parvenu à s’imposer durablement au plus haut niveau. Après trois splits compliqués, il avait finalement été écarté du cinq de départ au profit de Sheo, avant de passer plusieurs mois sans compétition officielle. Son arrivée chez Solary pourrait donc lui offrir l’occasion de relancer sa carrière.

Le défi s’annonce toutefois particulièrement relevé pour Boukada, tant Solary a impressionné en 2026. Présente en LFL depuis 2019, la structure a enfin décroché ses premiers titres nationaux, remportant notamment le LFL Invitational et le Spring Split, sans oublier son sacre aux EMEA Masters Winter. Les Tourangeaux ont également brillé sur la scène internationale en atteignant la finale du premier World Star Challengers Invitational, où ils se sont inclinés de justesse face à T1 (2-3). Une année exceptionnelle, malgré plusieurs revers contre Galions dans la deuxième partie de saison.

Au cœur de cette réussite, Zicssi s’est imposé comme l’un des meilleurs junglers du circuit européen secondaire. Ses performances pourraient désormais lui ouvrir les portes du LEC, avec SK Gaming comme destination privilégiée à ce stade. Pour Solary, son éventuel départ représenterait une perte importante, mais le recrutement de Boukada témoignerait de la volonté du club de rester compétitif malgré les incertitudes entourant l’avenir de la LFL. Reste à savoir si l’ancien joueur de Shifters parviendra à retrouver son meilleur niveau et à faire oublier son prédécesseur.

title: Fortnite Crew Changes December 5: More V-Bucks the Longer You Stay, No More Monthly Skins
content:
Fortnite Crew is changing on December 5, 2026. Epic Games is ending the monthly Crew Pack outfits and replacing them with more V-Bucks the longer you stay subscribed, starting at 1,000 a month and rising to 1,600 after a year. Subscribers also get a 20% XP boost. The price stays at $11.99 a month, according to Epic’s announcement on Fortnite.com .

For many players this is a bigger change than it looks. Epic cut Crew’s monthly allowance from 1,000 to 800 V-Bucks from June 6, 2026, as we reported in our story on the Fortnite Crew V-Bucks drop to 800 . The new system brings the starting amount back to 1,000 and goes higher from the third month.

Your monthly V-Bucks now depend on how long you have been subscribed, across four tiers.

By our count, a new subscriber who stays for a full year would get 15,600 V-Bucks in the first 12 months. That is 6,000 more than the 9,600 a year the 800 V-Bucks allowance gives, and 3,600 more than the old 1,000 a month. From the second year, Gold members would get 19,200 V-Bucks a year.

The monthly Crew Pack outfits are ending. December 2026 is the last month of exclusive Crew skins under the current system. Players who already own Crew Pack outfits will receive all of their remaining Legacy Styles for those outfits, pickaxes and back blings, so nothing they own is lost.

The OG Pass is also leaving Crew. Fortnite OG’s current season ends on December 5, and the next OG era is planned for late 2027.

title: Pokimane and Atrioc Deepfake Controversy Explained: Full Timeline From 2023 to 2026
content:
Pokimane has reopened the Atrioc deepfake controversy more than three years after it first broke. On an October 25, 2026 stream, she said that seeing Atrioc’s name or face causes her “a lot of discomfort and anxiety,” and the next day she explained on X that the deepfake page shown on his stream in 2023 was of her. Atrioc responded on October 27, calling her feelings “totally valid” and saying he had pulled out of a planned TwitchCon appearance this year.

Here is everything that has happened between the two streamers, from the January 2023 stream that started it to this week.

In late January 2023, Atrioc, whose real name is Brandon Ewing, showed a browser tab on his Twitch stream for a website that sold sexual AI deepfakes of female streamers. Pokimane, Maya Higa and QTCinderella were among the women on the site, and Sweet Anita later found her name connected to it too. We reported at the time that Atrioc had been caught paying for deepfakes of fellow streamers .

Atrioc apologised on stream on January 30, 2023. He admitted he had paid for access to the site, said he found it through an ad while reading about AI and deepfake technology, and said it was a one-time visit. He stepped back from streaming and from Offbrand, the agency he co-founded with Ludwig Ahgren and others.

QTCinderella, a close friend of Atrioc before the incident, spoke out as the clip spread. She said being seen naked against your will “should NOT BE A PART OF THIS JOB,” and she later ended the friendship.

To help the women affected, Atrioc sent $60,000 to a law firm to cover legal fees for takedown requests against sites hosting the deepfakes, and worked with Ceartas, a company that files takedown notices, according to his Wikipedia page . He returned to streaming in March 2023.

title: LEC : Vitality ouvre la porte au départ de Naak Nako
content:
Le mercato s’annonce particulièrement agité du côté de Vitality. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , la structure française serait prête à écouter les offres pour Kaan « Naak Nako » Okan, pourtant sous contrat jusqu’à fin 2027. Plusieurs organisations auraient déjà manifesté leur intérêt, notamment G2 Esports, Movistar KOI et Natus Vincere. Mais pour autoriser son joueur à discuter avec d’autres équipes, Vitality réclamerait initialement un engagement financier de 350 000 euros, applicable si les négociations aboutissent. Un montant élevé, qui ne constitue toutefois pas une clause de départ fixe et pourrait être revu à la baisse selon les offres.

Cette situation illustre la cote grandissante du jeune toplaner sur la scène européenne. Arrivé en LEC en 2025 après être passé par l’académie de Vitality, Naak Nako s’est rapidement imposé parmi les talents les plus prometteurs à son poste. Élu MVP de la saison régulière du Spring Split 2026 et sélectionné dans la première équipe type du championnat, le Turc a confirmé son potentiel malgré les résultats irréguliers de son équipe. Dès le mois d’août, Fabien « Neo » Devide, président de Vitality, n’excluait d’ailleurs pas un départ : « Nous verrons en fonction du contexte et des opportunités. Tout est ouvert, mais pour l’instant, Naak Nako est un joueur de Vitality jusqu’à fin 2027. »

Les trois principaux prétendants présentent des situations bien différentes. Chez G2, l’avenir de BrokenBlade reste incertain malgré une proposition de prolongation formulée depuis plusieurs semaines. Le club explorerait donc plusieurs options, sans pour autant avoir définitivement renoncé à conserver son capitaine. Movistar KOI pourrait également envisager un changement après une saison compliquée pour Myrwn, tandis que NAVI chercherait à renforcer sa toplane pour franchir un nouveau cap en LEC. Avec le contrat de Maynter qui arrive à expiration, l’organisation ukrainienne disposerait notamment d’une opportunité pour revoir son effectif.

Du côté de Vitality, un éventuel transfert s’inscrirait dans une reconstruction plus large. Après le départ attendu de Lyncas vers G2 et celui de Pad, la structure française devrait accueillir un nouveau staff composé de Wadi au poste d’entraîneur principal et de Reha comme strategic coach. Des essais auraient déjà été organisés avec plusieurs joueurs du LEC et des ligues régionales, une démarche encore peu courante à ce niveau. Pour autant, rien n’est encore décidé concernant Naak Nako, qui pourrait parfaitement poursuivre l’aventure chez Vitality. Son avenir s’annonce néanmoins comme l’un des dossiers majeurs de ce mercato européen.

title: LEC : G2 a trouvé le remplaçant de SkewMond
content:
Le mercato s’emballe chez G2 Esports. Alors que Sheep Esports révélait ce mercredi que Rudy « SkewMond » Semaan ne serait pas conservé dans le cinq de départ pour 2027, la structure européenne aurait déjà identifié son remplaçant. Il s’agirait de Linas « Lyncas » Nauncikas, actuel jungler de Vitality, qui devrait rejoindre les champions d’Europe à l’ouverture du marché des transferts. Le Lituanien de 22 ans était particulièrement convoité durant cette intersaison, avec des intérêts de Fnatic, Team Heretics, GIANTX et Vitality, qui espérait le conserver. Mais c’est finalement le projet de G2 qui aurait remporté la mise.

Un choix qui ne manque pas de surprendre, tant SkewMond sort d’une saison remarquable. Avec le Français dans ses rangs, G2 a remporté les trois titres du LEC en 2026, réalisant un Golden Road historique sur la scène européenne. Élu MVP de la finale du Spring Split, SkewMond s’était également illustré sur la scène internationale, notamment lors du First Stand. Mais après une nouvelle désillusion aux Worlds, conclus dès le Swiss Stage avec un bilan de 1-3, les Samouraïs ont décidé de changer de jungler malgré le contrat du Français, valable jusqu’en 2028.

L’arrivée attendue de Lyncas serait également synonyme de retrouvailles avec Patrick « Pad » Suckow-Breum. L’entraîneur danois, lui aussi en provenance de Vitality, devrait rejoindre G2 en tant que strategic coach pour la saison prochaine. Les deux hommes entretiennent une relation privilégiée depuis plusieurs années, Lyncas ayant notamment quitté la Karmine Corp en 2024 pour travailler à ses côtés. « Pad et moi sommes très proches » , confiait d’ailleurs le jungler à Sheep Esports en février dernier. Une complicité qui pourrait faciliter son intégration au sein de sa nouvelle équipe.

Sur le plan sportif, Lyncas sort d’une saison encourageante malgré les difficultés collectives de Vitality. Régulièrement compétitive en saison régulière, notamment au Spring Split, la formation française n’a jamais réussi à confirmer en playoffs. Le Lituanien s’est néanmoins distingué individuellement, intégrant la troisième équipe type du Spring Split, derrière SkewMond et Yike. Il avait également montré de belles choses lors de la Demacia Cup, où Vitality avait pris deux manches d’avance face à KT Rolster avant de finalement s’incliner (2-3). Désormais attendu chez G2, Lyncas aura la lourde tâche de succéder à l’un des meilleurs junglers européens de 2026, avec l’ambition d’aider les Samouraïs à retrouver les sommets internationaux.

title: Gen.G sweep LYON to end North America’s Worlds 2026 run and set up iG semi-final
content:
Gen.G beat LYON 3-0 in Allen, Texas, removing North America's last team from Worlds 2026. The LCK top seed are now one series from a first Worlds final, with a revived Invictus Gaming in the way.

Gen.G swept LYON in the second Worlds 2026 quarter-final in Allen, Texas. The defeat removes North America’s last team from the tournament. The LCK top seed now face Invictus Gaming in a best-of-five semi-final on Saturday, starting at 16:00 Central Time.

Reaching the last four secures Gen.G at least third or fourth place. That is a familiar stopping point for the organisation. It has finished third or fourth at four of its last five Worlds and has never played in a Worlds final, GosuGamers reported.

The stakes go beyond one team. Gen.G entered the tournament as the LCK’s top seed. Korean sides are chasing a fifth Summoner’s Cup in a row.

Their opponents bring their own history. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 in the opening quarter-final. That put iG into their first Worlds semi-final since 2019. TheShy and Rookie, who won Worlds with iG in 2018, are back in the last four.

The money rises sharply from here. Worlds 2026 carries a US$5,000,000 prize pool. The champion takes US$1,000,000 (20%), and the runner-up receives US$800,000.

title: Worlds 2026 : pas de miracle pour LYON, balayé 3-0 par Gen.G
content:
Dernier représentant de l’Amérique du Nord encore en lice, LYON espérait créer l’exploit devant son public à Allen, au Texas. Mais face à l’armada coréenne, Inspired et ses coéquipiers ont rapidement déchanté. Dès la première manche, Canyon a imposé son rythme avec une Qiyana dévastatrice (6/1/6), multipliant les interventions sur la toplane pour mettre Dhokla en difficulté. À ses côtés, Kiin a également livré une prestation impressionnante sur Olaf (6/1/7), transformant le haut de la carte en véritable cauchemar pour les Américains. Malgré un début de partie encourageant de Berserker sur la botlane, LYON n’a jamais réussi à inverser la tendance et Gen.G a logiquement ouvert le score.

La deuxième manche a tourné à la démonstration. En seulement 26 minutes, les champions coréens ont balayé leurs adversaires avec un score de 22 éliminations à 6. Intouchable sur son Sion (4/0/8), Kiin a une nouvelle fois dominé les affrontements, tandis que la combinaison Ashe-Séraphine a parfaitement fonctionné sur la botlane. En face, Isles a tenté de créer des opportunités avec son Pyke, mais ses initiatives trop audacieuses ont souvent été sanctionnées. Complètement dépassé dans les combats collectifs, LYON n’a trouvé aucune solution pour ralentir la machine Gen.G, désormais à une seule victoire de la qualification.

LA FLÈCHE EST PIXEL WOW ! pic.twitter.com/J9JjiMdahj

Dos au mur, les Nord-Américains ont décidé de tenter le tout pour le tout dans la troisième manche. Avec notamment un Gangplank inattendu pour Dhokla, LYON a proposé une draft audacieuse et affiché un visage bien plus combatif. Pourtant malmené en début de partie, le toplaner américain a progressivement trouvé son utilité dans les teamfights, permettant à son équipe de prendre ponctuellement l’avantage. Pour la première fois de la série, Inspired et ses partenaires ont véritablement réussi à bousculer les favoris du tournoi, laissant entrevoir la possibilité de prolonger le suspense.

Mais Gen.G disposait de trop d’armes pour se laisser surprendre. Dans les affrontements décisifs du midgame, Chovy et Ruler ont repris le contrôle, faisant parler leur maîtrise collective pour éteindre les derniers espoirs de LYON. Après 33 minutes, les Coréens ont définitivement validé leur qualification sur un score sans appel de 3-0. Gen.G retrouvera désormais Invictus Gaming en demi-finale, après la victoire des Chinois face à Top Esports (3-1). Une affiche particulièrement prometteuse, avec notamment un duel de prestige sur la midlane entre Chovy et son compatriote Rookie. De quoi offrir un nouveau grand rendez-vous aux amateurs de League of Legends.

Inspired est en train de débiter pic.twitter.com/SQjN9ZcAQE

title: WoW Forever now live with Skyborne, dungeons, and new Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor zones
content:
World of Warcraft: Forever (WoW Forever) is now live, allowing players to enjoy some nostalgia yet also explore a reimagined Azeroth.

WoW Forever launched on Nov. 4, allowing players to check out new and reimagined zones across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. These include areas such as the Riverglades and Zephras Isle. Players can also take on more than 1,000 quests across their level 1 to 60 journey.

Zephras Isle, in particular, is the starting zone for Skyborne champions. Those who wish to create their own Skyborne character can choose between the Alliance and Horde. In terms of playable Skyborne classes at launch, they are Druid, Hunter, Mage, Rogue, and Warrior for the Alliance and Druid, Hunter, Rogue, Shaman, and Warrior for the Horde.

As for the new dungeons, WoW Forever introduces nine of them at launch. These require five players each and become available at level 13. Raids, meanwhile, unlock on Dec. 9.

World of Warcraft Interviews WoW Forever interview: Michael Nuthals on bringing the magic of 2004 Azeroth into 2026 An interview with Blizzard about how WoW Forever brings the magic of Classic into 2026 through raids, dungeons, zones, and...

When does WoW Forever take place? Those who are interested in how WoW Forever fits into the timeline, Blizzard Entertainment revealed that it’s set after Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom and before Molten Core.

As a Tier 3 Dota 2 tournament , EPL Masters III primarily features teams that rarely get the opportunity to compete in the game’s biggest events. Yellow Submarine, however, should not be underestimated. Under the management of Team Spirit, the CIS team became the incubator of talent in the region, producing a new generation of world-class players like Alan “Satanic” Gallyamov and Bohdan “Batyuk” Batiuk.

Both teams in the lower bracket final of EPL Masters III experience their respective setbacks in the tournament, with Yellow Submarine losing to Natus Vincere at the upper bracket final, while GamerLegion falls earlier in the lower bracket after Natus Vincere takes them down.

NAVI appears to be in top shape all around the tourney, defeating every team in their path to the grand final without dropping a single match. Despite their disappointing performance at PARI Universe, the young lineup, mostly made up of players in their early 20s, has already shown plenty of potential with runner-up finishes at PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM 6.

title: PS Store Black Friday Deals Aren’t the Same for Everyone, No Explanations Why
content:
PlayStation Store’s Black Friday sale is barely a day old, and some PS5 owners are already finding out that the discount on their screen is not the one their friends are getting.

Screenshots from players’ accounts, shared on X by Pirat_Nation on 4 November, show Astro Bot and Death Stranding 2: On the Beach selling at clearly different prices on different accounts during the same promotion. The pattern has surfaced in earlier sales over the past year, but its return for Black Friday, the busiest shopping window on the calendar, means far more buyers are likely to run into it.

Sony’s dynamic pricing is affecting PS Store Black Friday deals, with different players getting different prices for the same games. Astro Bot ranges from $33.59 to $39.59, while Death Stranding 2 goes from $34.29 to $39.89 depending on the account. Sony hasn’t explained why… pic.twitter.com/XiAoIYeDsR

On one account, Astro Bot is listed at $39.59, which is 34% off its $59.99 original price, while a second account shows the same standard edition at $33.59, a much deeper 44% discount. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach follows the same pattern. One account sees $39.89, or 43% off $69.99, while another sees $34.29 at 51% off, which leaves a $5.60 gap for an identical digital copy.

Deals account CAG, which posts on X as @videogamedeals, flagged the same Astro Bot split earlier that day, adding a blunt note that the price depends on your account. The timing in the screenshots also lines up with Sony’s own schedule. The Astro Bot listing says the offer ends on 21 November at 1:59am Central time, which matches the 20 November, 23:59 PST cut-off Sony set for deals that leave early.

Sony’s official PlayStation Blog post , written by Promotions Proposal Manager Zack Garvey, says the Black Friday Deals began on 4 November with up to 75% off thousands of PS5, PS4 and PS VR2 games. The promotion refreshes with new titles on 16 November and runs until 30 November. Astro Bot even appears in the blog’s own preview of discounted games, and our full PlayStation Black Friday 2026 games list covers the rest of the sale. Sony’s small print warns that the promotion and its percentage discounts may differ by region. However, it says nothing about prices changing from one account to another inside the same region, which is exactly what these players are describing.

title: Marvel Takes Over Burger King India: Green Whoppers, Black Buns and Thor Nuggets
content:
Burger King India has handed its menu over to Doctor Doom. Its Avengers: Doomsday collection coats burgers, nuggets, wings and fries in a bright green spicy garlic sauce and swaps the usual Whopper bun for a glossy black one.

The chain announced on the evening of 4 November that the “Burger King India X Avengers: Doomsday Collection” was available across all of its restaurants in India. That followed a week of teasers that began on 30 October, and the launch artwork pairs the Marvel Studios Avengers: Doomsday logo with a Burger King logo recoloured in green.

Two universes. One epic collaboration. Burger King India is joining forces with Avengers Doomsday for something BIG. And trust us, this is just the beginning. Stay tuned. We’re just getting started… #BurgerKing #AvengersDoomsday #DoomsdayCollection #DoctorDoom #Marvel pic.twitter.com/UqixBX4IKT

Ten items make up the range, and BK India’s own menu descriptions say almost all of them are “dunked” in the same spicy garlic sauce. The two headline burgers are the Doomsday Whopper Extra Crunchy Veg at ₹199 and the Doomsday Whopper Flame-Grilled Chicken at ₹239, both served in what BK calls a premium black glazed bun.

Three more burgers borrow their names from heroes and villains in the film. The Cyclops Soft Paneer Burger costs ₹219, the Loki Molten Cheese Burger is ₹239 and the Magneto Crunchy Chicken Burger sits at ₹229, with all three served in black glazed brioche buns. The sides follow the same formula, so nothing escapes the green treatment. Shuri Vibranium Fries cost ₹159 and come with the garlic sauce plus a black sprinkle, while Thor Thunder Nuggets are ₹109 for four pieces or ₹169 for six.

Chicken fans also get Falcon Fearless Chicken Wings at ₹209 for four pieces, along with Gambit Boneless Chicken at ₹199 for four or ₹299 for seven. Washing it all down is Fantastic Fizz, a sweet lime and lemon drink that runs from ₹112 for a small to ₹154 for a large.

title: GE Bundle Is Leaving Valorant Forever, and 11 November Is Your Last Chance to Own It
content:
Riot Games is pulling the VCT Team Capsules from the Valorant store on 11 November, and for Global Esports supporters this is the final chance to buy their team’s in-game bundle.

The official VALORANT Champions Tour account set the cut-off on 4 November, saying the capsules leave the store worldwide at 10am Pacific Time. Its graphic, headed “TEAM CAPSULES LEAVING SOON”, shows LOUD’s green and black Classic skin alongside the matching gun buddy.

Because US clocks went back on 1 November, that deadline falls at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 11 November. For fans elsewhere, it works out to 19:00 CET in central Europe, 23:30 IST in India and 03:00 on Thursday 12 November in Seoul and Tokyo. Global Esports quote-posted the announcement a few hours later with a much blunter message for its fans. “Truly the last time you can buy the GE Bundle, ever,” the Indian organisation wrote, before telling supporters to get theirs while they still can.

Truly the last time you can buy the GE Bundle, ever. Get yours while you can. https://t.co/0raJ23y40G

In GE’s case, the word “ever” is meant literally. Founder and CEO Rushindra Sinha posted a farewell video on 19 October, and the organisation then released its entire Valorant roster as it closed its competitive operations.

The timing still stings, because GE had only just won VCT Pacific Stage 2 in Busan in September with a 3-2 reverse sweep of Nongshim RedForce. Sinha has said the brand will carry on as GE Studios, an AI-focused venture, rather than as an esports team.

title: Razer’s asking $350 for a “Magnesium Alloyed” Limited PS5 Controller
content:
Razer has put a price on PlayStation obsession, and it is a steep one. The Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition , unveiled on 3 November, wraps Razer’s flagship PS5 controller in a magnesium alloy exoskeleton and caps the first run at 1,337 individually serialised units worldwide.

According to launch details Razer shared with outlets including TechRadar, GamesRadar+ and Game Rant, the pad costs $349.99 in the US, £349.99 in the UK and €368.99 in Europe, with sales opening on 10 November. Razer’s own product page does not show a price yet and only offers a Notify Me button, while its official X post says the countdown begins on 6 November.

Razer says the controller will be sold only through Razer.com and select RazerStore locations, and GamesRadar+ reports that stock will go out in regionalised drops on a first-come, first-served basis. Razer has not said whether buyers will be limited to one unit each, which matters a great deal when 1,337 units are split across the whole planet.

That number is the old internet spelling of “leet”, and Razer has used it before. Its Huntsman Signature Edition keyboard was unveiled in February in a run of 1,337 serialised units, and it now shows as out of stock at US$499.99 on Razer’s US store.

Meet the Razer Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition, a new expression of competitive mastery that takes shape around a magnesium alloy exoskeleton: https://t.co/GCzl87zpIB Every detail serves a purpose, from its laser-etched glass touchpad to its micro-textured TPU grips. Anti-drift… pic.twitter.com/crDbznuZlH

The standard Raiju V3 Pro sells for $219.99 on Razer’s US store, so the Signature Edition asks for $130 more. Judging by Razer’s own spec lists, most of that money goes into materials and finish rather than new performance hardware, since the core layout and sensors carry over.

title: Sam Altman Becomes ‘Ram Altman’, Says His PC RAM Comments Were Taken Out of Context
content:
Sam Altman has spent the past week discovering that PC gamers do not take kindly to being told their RAM would be better off in a data centre. On Wednesday, the OpenAI chief executive hit back, insisting his remarks had been taken out of context and agreeing to a fan’s request to rename himself “Ram Altman” on X.

His clearest defence came in a reply posted shortly after 05:00 UTC on 4 November. “I actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers,” Altman wrote. He went on to call it “f***ing annoying that this was taken out of context”, adding that he has “been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time”.

but only because…i actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is fucking annoying that this was taken out of context. i have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time.

The rebrand itself started as a joke in the replies. When one user asked him to “rename your x to ram altman!”, Altman simply answered “ok yeah”. Within hours, other users were asking why his display name now read “Ram Altman”, although by Wednesday evening UTC the profile was back to plain Sam Altman.

A few hours before that exchange, he had already tried a shorter version of the same message. Replying to a user who asked “why u want my ram then”, Altman posted “I want you to have so much RAM” before adding “let’s build more”.

The comments that started the row came on Cheeky Pint, the interview show hosted by Stripe co-founder John Collison, in an episode published on YouTube on 29 October. While discussing bottlenecks in the AI supply chain, Altman pointed out that making memory had rarely been a great business over the long run. Now, he said, the big producers are “each going to make like $100 billion of free cash flow in a year.”

title: Jonathan Gaming Hits 8 Million YouTube Subscribers
content:
Jonathan Gaming has crossed 8 million subscribers on YouTube, and the Team Apex Gaming founder marked the moment by turning his milestone stream into a full Halloween party. He went live on the night of 4 November dressed as a vampire, and his channel was showing 8.02 million subscribers as the broadcast wrapped up in the early hours of 5 November.

The stream, titled “8 MILLION SPECIAL | JONATHAN IS BACK! | BGMI!”, started just after 9pm IST on his main channel and ran for five and a half hours. Its thumbnail had already set the mood, with blood-red “8M” lettering, jack-o’-lanterns and a full moon framing Jonathan in his number 16 jersey.

Clips from the night spread quickly among fans on X. They show Jonathan in a high-collared cape and red waistcoat, a Halloween-style cake, friends crowding around him, skeleton props in the background and a live counter ticking past 8,000,000.

The celebration also drew a big audience of its own, since YouTube’s counter showed the broadcast had passed 2.1 million views by the time it ended. For a creator who now splits his time between competing and running an organisation, that suggests his core audience has stayed with him through a year of upheaval.

Jonathan’s growth is unusually easy to track, because he has marked almost every million with a special video or stream on his channel. His 1 million special went up on 8 July 2020, and he celebrated 2 million live on 10 March 2021.

The next day, he told fans in a post on X that reaching a “2 Million naughty family” was “a dream come true”. The jumps that followed came quickly, with his 3 million special on 22 September 2021 and his 4 million special on 13 April 2022.

title: FISSURE CEO Admits It Still Owes CS2 and Dota 2 Prize Money, Eyes Q1 2027 for Next Big Payout
content:
FISSURE chief executive Nikolay Vesnin has admitted that the organiser still owes CS2 and Dota 2 prize money, and he has named the first quarter of 2027 for its next big repayment.

The admission came in an open letter published on FISSURE’s website on 4 November, in which he apologised “to the teams and players who are still waiting for their prize money.” “In short: we acknowledge the debt in full,” he wrote, adding that payments have run since the summer, that about half the CS2 debt is cleared and that Dota 2 payments began in October.

Recently, many questions have been raised regarding outstanding prize money payments for our CS2 and Dota 2 tournaments. We understand the concerns of players, teams, and the community, and we acknowledge our responsibility for the current situation. pic.twitter.com/Fo11yOGy8s

The letter gives no total, and Vesnin says he does not want to “announce unconfirmed amounts”, so the clearest record of who is owed remains a disclosure page that FISSURE published on 23 June.

That page names 15 Counter-Strike organisations: TYLOO, MIBR, FURIA, Lynn Vision, Wildcard, Team Falcons, G2, 3DMAX, The MongolZ, Team Liquid, paiN Gaming, Astralis, Aurora, GamerLegion and Legacy. It attaches no event or amount to any name, yet it includes both 2025 Playground champions, TYLOO and FURIA, plus Astralis and The MongolZ, whom they beat in the July and September finals .

On 5 November the page still listed all 15 teams, even though it promises updates “as obligations are settled” and Vesnin says about half of the CS2 money has already been paid. FISSURE has published no similar list for Dota 2. In July, though, Russian outlet Esports.ru reported that Anton “dyrachyo” Shkredov, who won FISSURE Playground 1 with Tundra Esports in 2025, had said on stream that he was paid only a quarter of his winnings.

title: Ukraine Takes FIFA Match-Fixing Ring to Court as ESportsBattle Questions Reach ESIC
content:
Ukrainian prosecutors have taken a cyberfootball match-fixing case to court, and the fallout is now reaching one of the busiest betting-focused esports circuits in the world. One player has already been convicted of throwing ESports Battle Football matches on FIFA, and the case has raised fresh questions about how that competition is policed.

On 30 October, the Office of the Prosecutor General said it had sent an indictment to court against a 28-year-old Kyiv resident and two cyberfootball players. According to the office’s official Telegram channel , the organiser agreed match results with players in advance and paid them to lose, so that the group could profit from bets.

Prosecutors say the scheme ran during 2022 and 2023, with bets placed at both legal and illegal bookmakers, including some registered in Asian countries. The three defendants were notified of suspicion in August, and they face charges under Article 369-3 of Ukraine’s Criminal Code, which covers unlawful influence on the results of official sports competitions.

The investigation also crossed borders, with searches in Spain and Germany in September carried out with the help of Interpol, Europol and local police. Officers seized phones, computer equipment and handwritten notes during those raids. Two further suspects have been notified, and authorities are deciding whether to put them on an international wanted list.

Prosecutors added that one member of the group had already been convicted of deliberately losing FIFA matches for betting, and that the verdict is now final. That description matches the earlier case of Serhiy Kryvenko, although the new indictment does not name him.

Kryvenko’s case, reported by Censor.net in July citing the Prosecutor General’s Office, involved a six-person group of an organiser, a co-organiser and four players. It operated from November 2022 to October 2024 and placed bets on predetermined results in the ESports Battle Football tournament.

title: NS RedForce Replace Dambi With UdoTan, the Duelist Who Reverse-Swept Them in Busan
content:
NS RedForce have signed Go “UdoTan” Kyung-won, the South Korean duelist who reverse-swept them in the VCT Pacific Stage 2 grand final in Busan only two months ago. The club confirmed the deal on November 4, just a day after saying goodbye to Masters Santiago MVP Dambi .

In its official announcement on X, NS said UdoTan will “spearhead the team with his relentless pushes and explosive firepower”, which leaves little doubt about the job he has been hired to do. That is the language of an entry duelist, and it describes exactly the hole Dambi’s Neon left in the lineup when his time at the club ended.

Sheep Esports first reported the move on October 23, so the announcement confirms one of the worst-kept secrets of the Pacific off-season. Even so, the deal carries a sharp twist, because NS are bringing in the player who did the most damage to them in the biggest match of their year.

[OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT] #VALORANT 𝐖𝐞𝐥𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞, 𝐔𝐝𝐨𝐓𝐚𝐧 'UdoTan' has signed to join the NS RedForce Valorant team. Please look forward to and show your support for 'UdoTan', who will spearhead the team with his relentless pushes and explosive firepower. 'UdoTan' 고경원… pic.twitter.com/7sYzHynIfN

UdoTan’s route to this point has been unusually long. According to VLR.gg, he debuted in 2020 and spent his early years with smaller sides such as GoNGo Prince, TALON and Gwangju Shadow, before moving to China with Four Angry Men in late 2023.

His breakthrough came with Rare Atom in 2024, when he finished runner-up at Ascension China while mostly playing initiator. Global Esports, the Indian organisation led by founder and CEO Rushindra Sinha, then signed him on October 31, 2024, and he soon became the team’s main duelist in VCT Pacific.

title: RNTX Jumps Into EA FC With Vanshaj Sharma, Two Days Before FC Pro’s London Qualifier
content:
RNTX has made its first known move into EA SPORTS FC, signing Indian player Vanshaj Sharma only two days before the FC Pro Open Global Qualifier gets under way in London. The organisation, which posts on X as Revenant Esports, confirmed on November 4 that he will represent it at the event.

The announcement went out at 11:02am IST with a welcome graphic that carries FC Pro branding, Indian flags and the logos of AMD Ryzen and Radeon, Monster Energy and Cybeart. RNTX called Vanshaj its representative for the qualifier, which starts on Friday, November 6, at BBC Television Studios.

MAKE WAY FOR @V_SHARMA10 ! Our rep in the FC Pro Open Global Qualifier starting November 6th in London! #WolvenSpark #RNTX pic.twitter.com/ek9QVtH7yL

His ticket to London had already been earned before the move was made public. Vanshaj came through the Asia South Regional Qualifier last month, and EA’s official list of 64 competitors names him alongside GodLike’s Charanjot Singh, so both of the region’s places went to Indian players.

Most fans in India still think of RNTX as a Battlegrounds Mobile India organisation before anything else. Revenant Esports and Team XSpark joined forces in October 2024, and only this week the organisation brought back in-game leader Shadow while BGMS Season 5 champion Phoenix joined its new BGMI lineup .

Its X profile also lists teams in Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, Brawl Stars and Call of Duty: Mobile, yet Liquipedia’s EA SPORTS FC wiki has no earlier record of the organisation in the game. Football esports is also a different kind of project, because FC Pro is a one-versus-one PlayStation 5 circuit where a single player carries the badge.

title: SEA Games 2027 More Than Doubles Its Esports Programme to a Record 13 Medal Events as Free Fire Bows Out
content:
The Southeast Asian Games Federation (SEAGF) has approved 13 esports medal events for the 34th SEA Games in Malaysia, the largest esports programme in the Games’ history and more than double Thailand’s six in December 2025.

The list was signed off at SEAGF Executive Committee Meeting No. 3 (2025-2027) on Friday, 30 October, which was chaired by Dr Nur Azmi Ahmad, deputy president of the Olympic Council of Malaysia. According to Bernama , member nations joined by online conference and raised no objections to the sports selected.

That meeting approved 473 events across 43 sports for the Games, which run from 18 to 29 September 2027 across four clusters in Kuala Lumpur, Sarawak, Penang and Johor. Esports sits in Category II of the official list, the group reserved for sports that also feature at the Olympic Games, the Asian Games or the Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games.

The programme is split into 11 men’s events and two women’s events, with no mixed category at all. That marks a clear break from Thailand, where Free Fire and FC Online were both contested as mixed team events.

Two of those events still carry a question mark, because the list names Gran Turismo 7 for one racing medal but gives no game for the solo and duo “E-Racing Track” events.

The host federation had flagged this expansion well before the October meeting. In February, Malaysia Electronic Sports Federation (MESF) president Muhammad Naim Al Amin Saharudin told Bernama that his federation would propose more than 10 titles, including racing simulators never contested at the Games before.

title: CS Legend shox hospitalized with abdominal pain
content:
Richard “shox” Papillon, one of the most decorated players France has produced in Counter-Strike, is in hospital being treated for what he understands to be a fairly serious intra-abdominal infection. The 34-year-old has spent several days on intravenous antibiotics, and doctors are now running a series of checks ahead of an endoscopy and a colonoscopy.

The news first reached fans through his Instagram account, before shox addressed it on X on 1 November with a short post written in French. In our translation, he told followers that “there was a little glitch in Beijing, I’m in for several days on drips,” and he even joked that his famous luck seemed to have deserted him. He added that doctors were treating him and that he expected to have further tests back in France, before closing with a simple message for worried fans: “Rest assured, I’m OK.”

Yo les potes, si vous etiez pas au courant via insta, ya eu un petit bug a Beijing, jen ai pour plusieurs jours de perfs (où est passée la chatte légendaire de riri? ) Ils me guerissent et ensuite je devrais faire des examens complementaires en France. Rassurez vous ca va… pic.twitter.com/W8jUc4xy49

A longer update followed on Instagram this week, and the CS2 News account relayed it in English on 4 November. According to that translation, the trouble began with pain in his side, and he stressed that he still did not have all the information about his condition. As far as he knew, it was a fairly serious infection inside the abdomen, and he had been on IV antibiotics for around three days to bring the inflammation down.

Doctors have since ordered what he described as a whole battery of tests, starting with an electrocardiogram. They are also checking whether his body can handle a general anaesthetic, because an endoscopy and a colonoscopy are planned to investigate the problem further. Shox admitted that he did not yet know whether he would need to stay on antibiotics once those results came back.

He also explained why he had said so little until now, telling fans that he simply had not had the energy to post during the first few days of treatment. Beyond those details, shox has not shared a diagnosis or any timeline for his recovery. Fans have been leaving get-well messages in the replies to his X post, which had passed 100,000 views by 4 November.

title: Lyncas Set to Join G2 Esports for LEC 2027, Replacing Spring Finals MVP SkewMond
content:
G2 Esports are reportedly ready to change a winning formula. According to Sheep Esports, Team Vitality jungler Linas “Lyncas” Nauncikas is set to join G2 for the 2027 LEC season, replacing Rudy “SkewMond” Semaan after a year in which G2 won every domestic title on offer.

Neither G2 nor Lyncas had confirmed the move at the time of writing, and it cannot become official just yet. Lyncas is under contract with Vitality until November 26, so he is expected to sign with G2 only once he becomes a free agent later this month.

On paper, the decision looks like a bold one for G2. With BrokenBlade, SkewMond, Caps, Hans Sama and Labrov, G2 won the LEC Versus, Spring and Summer titles in 2026, and SkewMond was named MVP of the Spring Finals after the 3-2 win over Karmine Corp.

International results told a very different story, however. G2 finished second at First Stand and fourth at MSI, went out early at the Esports World Cup and then left Worlds 2026 in the Swiss Stage with a 1-3 record after an unfavourable draw.

G2 have answered international disappointment this way before. After the 2024 season, the organisation moved on from jungler Martin “Yike” Sundelin and support Mihael “Mikyx” Mehle despite dominating Europe, and SkewMond and Labrov arrived in the lineup that followed.

This time, Sheep Esports reports that SkewMond will not continue on G2’s active roster in 2027, even though many regarded him as the team’s best performer this year. His contract with G2 runs until November 2028, according to Leaguepedia, so where the Frenchman plays next is still an open question.

title: Thieves hit BMIC 2026 backstage, Indian pro says cash stolen from Japanese pros too
content:
BMIC 2026 was meant to be KRAFTON India’s showcase to the rest of Asia, but it has now been hit by a theft scandal. Indian participant Gladiators Esports’ star Neyo has said that cash was stolen from player bags in the backstage area at the Dome in Mumbai, and that Japanese players lost money as well.

The BGMI International Cup ran from 30 October to 1 November at The Dome, SVP Indoor Stadium, NSCI. Six Indian teams faced five from South Korea and five from Japan there, with a ₹1 crore prize pool on the line. According to Neyo, the money went missing from an area where players had no choice but to leave their belongings while they were on stage.

Neyo explained that teams were required to leave their things on tables in the backstage area during matches, from bags and pillows to food. On Day 2, after his matches were over, he went back to his bag and found that a keychain he had been carrying, one that several people had complimented, was no longer there.

At that point, as Neyo describes, he did not think it was serious enough to push further, and he said he would check with the management instead. The bigger shock came only after the event had finished on 1 November, when another fellow player, Robin came to his room with news of his own. According to Neyo, Robin told him that ₹5,500 (about $50) had gone from his bag. That prompted Neyo to check his own wallet, and when he opened it, he said, “the whole cash was gone.” He put his own loss at around ₹9,500 (about $95), on top of the missing keychain. This incident is from the account of Gladiator Esports’ Neyo himself.

Neyo said the organisers, Tesseract Esports, are checking the CCTV footage from the backstage area and expect to update the players within one to two days. Neither KRAFTON India nor Tesseract Esports had made a public statement about the thefts at the time of writing, and no arrest or recovery has been reported.

The most damaging part of Neyo’s account concerns the visitors. He said that several Japanese players also found cash missing from their belongings, and that the money taken from them included Japanese currency.

title: Microsoft Is Giving Away an Xbox Series X Inside a Five Foot Alligator, But Only US Fans Can Win It
content:
Microsoft has built some strange Xbox Series X consoles over the years, but its latest one comes with teeth. The company has unveiled the Xbox Series X-BITE, a working Series X sealed inside a five-foot alligator, and one fan will get to take it home.

Announced on Xbox Wire on November 3, the one-off console is the prize in a social media sweepstakes that runs until November 10. It has also travelled well beyond the US, with searches for “xbox series” passing 10,000 in France on Wednesday, according to Google Trends.

Xbox sums up the idea in a single line: an alligator has swallowed an Xbox Series X whole, and the console still works. The creature measures more than five feet from snout to tail, and the console sits inside its body behind an illuminated Xbox Nexus.

The finishing touches lean fully into the joke. A custom Xbox Wireless Controller covered in bite marks rests between the alligator’s jaws, while its eyes have Xbox-green irises and pupils shaped like the Nexus logo.

Microsoft did not build the console in-house, turning instead to creature and animatronics specialist John Nolan Studio for the 3D modelling, sculpting and fabrication. The studio’s earlier work includes creatures for The Witcher, Jurassic World Dominion and HBO’s upcoming Harry Potter series.

The official rules still carry a sensible warning for whoever wins it. Microsoft calls the X-BITE “best as display only”, and it adds that no real alligators were used or harmed in the making of the console. Xbox has a long habit of turning its consoles into props for promotions. In 2024, it gave away a Deadpool & Wolverine Series X with a controller modelled on Deadpool’s backside, but Xbox itself describes the X-BITE as unlike anything it has made before.

title: Evil Esports Walk Out of Kronos Showmatches, Row Over India’s Eighth MLMS Slot Splits the MLBB Community
content:
India’s MOBA Legends scene has hit one of its biggest flashpoints in years. Evil Esports, one of the oldest names in Indian Mobile Legends, pulled out of a showmatch event run by caster Kronos on November 3, after a row over the schedule spiralled into public accusations of favouritism.

The showmatches were meant to help decide which team would be put forward for India’s eighth slot at the upcoming Google Play event that the community refers to as MLMS. The name goes back to the Moba Legends: 5v5! Master Series , whose first season earlier this year sent champions True Rippers to the Esports World Cup.

Instead of settling anything, Evil’s exit has turned a one-day event into a wider argument about how slots are handed out in Moba Legends: 5v5!, the version of Mobile Legends: Bang Bang played in India.

Evil’s place in that story runs deeper than most. The team was already billed as one of India’s top Mobile Legends squads before the game was banned in the country in June 2020. It was also still active when the title returned as Moba Legends: 5v5! under Vizta Games in April 2024.

Kronos, who runs the MOBA Masala Cup and whose channel also covers international events such as the North American Premier Series, put the showmatches together at short notice. Four teams were lined up, namely Yama Esports, Noctura, Daku Sena and Evil Esports, with Daku Sena widely seen as the frontrunners for the slot before Evil asked for a shot at it.

The trouble started with a clash between two versions of the schedule. A text version showed Evil playing two back-to-back best-of-three series, whereas the tournament graphic had them playing three in a row, and Kronos could not clear it up straight away because he was busy casting.

title: Major Fortnite Crew changes announced: No more skins and OG Pass removal
content:
Epic Games has revealed significant changes to the monthly Fortnite Crew subscription service. Beginning in December, players will no longer receive exclusive skins as part of the monthly offering, and the OG Pass will no longer be included.

These are merely the highlights of an otherwise surprising change to Fortnite Crew. Here’s everything we know about the situation.

Fortnite Crew skin (Image credit: Epic Games) The most unexpected change is removing skins exclusive to the Fortnite Crew membership. Since December 2020, Epic Games has released one skin every month for six years. Unfortunately, that will soon end.

The blog post reads, “Crew Pack Outfits are ending, and the final one will be December’s pack.” Many long-time subscribers have already voiced their concern with this decision, as it was one of the only worthwhile perks.

Moving forward, Fortnite Crew skins are gone, and it’s unclear whether any will return.

Fortnite Crew OG Pass (Image credit: Epic Games) Another bombshell revelation is that Fortnite OG is effectively going on a hiatus. Epic Games wrote, “OG Pass will end on December 5 with a dramatic conclusion at the end of Chapter 1: OG Season X,” adding that the next era of Fortnite OG drops in 2027.

title: Fortnite Pirate Shop Token Compass: Does it actually exist?
content:
Rumors in the Fortnite community suggest you can find a compass that helps you locate the ultra-rare Pirate Shop Token. Unfortunately, no such item exists in the game. It recently went viral because hundreds of thousands of players have spent countless hours searching for it.

This article outlines the compass’ origin and the latest updates regarding the mythical Pirate Shop Token.

As stated above, this rumored Fortnite compass doesn’t exist. It originated on TikTok, where creators claimed you can find it in-game and use it to locate a Chest containing the elusive Pirate Shop Token .

These videos usually depict a player with a compass displayed on-screen before they obtain the Pirate Shop Token. Several of these videos with similar images have surfaced since Epic Games released the Treasure Hunters season .

Many of these videos have generated hundreds of thousands of views, but they are all clickbait. One such post depicts a treasure-digging game where you can find the compass, and it will appear in your Fortnite locker.

Beyond the thousands of views generated, they also generate hundreds of comments. These comments have led trolls to respond that you can only find the compass during Fortnite “dev hours,” which leads to a “deez nuts” joke.

title: Call of Duty: Warzone Season 1 Brings Hajin, Zodiac and a Full Level Reset
content:
Call of Duty: Warzone Season 1 starts November 6 with the Hajin and Zodiac maps, a level reset, new field gear and Modern Warfare 4 weapons.

Call of Duty: Warzone Season 1 goes live at midnight ET on November 6 (2100 PT on November 5), adding two new maps and folding in Modern Warfare 4 content, Steam News reported in the season's official rundown.

Hajin, the new Battle Royale map, is the first in Call of Duty: Warzone set on the Korean Peninsula. Zodiac, a compact Resurgence map, is built around a drone factory in South Korea.

Hajin spans North and South Korea across 13 major points of interest. Hajin City has towering buildings and fortified roads, while Imjin Farmland is open ground suited to long-range fights.

North of the border are the 14th Political Prison, Chang-san Air Base and Deadtown.

Weather varies from clear skies to fog, wind and rain, and the map has two Gulag variants where eliminated players fight 1v1 to redeploy.

title: How to ‘Complete a Loot Radio Tower Side Op’ in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
content:
When you’re about halfway through the DMZ Orders in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , you’ll encounter a task to “Complete a Loot Radio Tower Side Op.” While this sounds simple enough, you might quickly realize that there is no “Loot Radio Tower” mission on the map, so where do you go to complete the Side Op?

Fortunately, we managed to complete this specific Side Op in MW4 DMZ , and we’ll explain exactly how to finish this DMZ Order.

With previous DMZ Orders, all you’ve had to do for missions like this one is look on the map and find a green icon labeled with the mission you’re trying to complete. However, there is no Loot Radio Tower mission labeled on any icon on the map, no matter how hard you look.

Instead, you need to head to one single spot on the map to complete this particular Side Op. Specifically, you need to go to “C6” quadrant in Hajin, which is located north of Deadtown . Here, just east of a Fire Station, you’ll see a blue radio tower that has red smoke coming off the top of it. If you don’t see red smoke, then another player has beaten you to this Side Op, so you’ll have to enter a new match to attempt it again.

When you spot the smoking radio tower, the “Loot Radio Tower” icon will appear on your map, giving you the go-ahead to complete the mission. To start, you need to climb the radio tower, which requires much more parkour than you’re used to in DMZ. You have to jump to poles, climb up ladders, and carefully make your way up the tower until you reach the top.

Once you reach the top, all you have to do is interact with the crate at the top of the tower, and it will complete the Loot Radio Tower Side Op in DMZ. You can loot the crate, which sometimes has decent loot, and after that, the DMZ Order task will be complete, and you can move on to the next one in MW4.

title: Modern Warfare 4 Review Roundup: Players Love the Campaign, Hate the Lobbies
content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has been on sale since 23 October, and the people playing it agree far more about one half of the game than the other. The campaign, which digital pre-order owners could start a week early on 16 October, has been welcomed as one of the best the series has produced. Multiplayer is a different conversation altogether, and most of the anger on Steam traces back to skill-based matchmaking, spawns and a launch map pool that few players are excited about.

We have not reviewed Modern Warfare 4 ourselves, so this roundup leans on what can be measured: Steam’s own review history, critic scores and the patch notes Infinity Ward has published since launch. The game costs $69.99 on Steam , or ₹4,999 in India, and it is out on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Nintendo Switch 2, with no version for PS4 or Xbox One. Infinity Ward leads development, while Beenox handled the PC version and Digital Legends built the Switch 2 edition , with Treyarch, Sledgehammer Games and Raven Software in support.

The Steam numbers show how quickly the mood changed. During the early access week, when only the story was playable, players left 5,238 positive reviews and 596 negative ones, so roughly nine in ten recommended it. Once multiplayer and DMZ opened on 23 October, however, the picture shifted. Since then the game has collected 3,137 positive and 2,244 negative reviews across all languages, a positive share of 58%, and the daily figure has stayed between roughly 48% and 64% the whole time. Across both periods it sits at 75% positive, while the English score on the store page reads Mostly Positive, with 73% of 5,738 reviews in favour as of 3 November.

That drop needs some context, though, because Modern Warfare 4 is still the best-received new Call of Duty on Steam in a long while. Its 73% among English reviews is ahead of Vanguard at 67%, Modern Warfare III at 46%, Modern Warfare II at 43%, Black Ops 6 at 42% and Black Ops 7 at 35%, and you have to go back to Black Ops III in 2015, which now sits at 90%, to find a yearly release that scores higher on the same store. Critics have been kinder still, with Metacritic listing the game at 85 overall, the PC version at 85, PS5 at 83 and Switch 2 at 86. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma went as far as calling it “one of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history” when she announced that the series had passed $40 billion in lifetime revenue .

Modern Warfare 4 closes out the rebooted Modern Warfare series that began in 2019, and it opens with North Korea invading the South. Much of the early story follows Private Park Hyun-jun, a young South Korean soldier whose squad is trying to hold the city of Hajin, while a second thread picks up where Modern Warfare III left off. Task Force 141 has broken up and Captain Price is on the run, with Ghost and Gaz under orders to bring him in. Price, meanwhile, is working off the books alongside Valeria Garza of the Las Almas Cartel, chasing a weapon on its way to a villain known as the Archer, played by Mads Mikkelsen, and CIA station chief Kate Laswell is still in touch with him.

Over 16 missions the story travels from Hajin to a New York nightclub, a car chase through Paris and a night raid in Mumbai, where Price and Gaz split into two teams. Mumbai later returns as one of the 12 core multiplayer maps, and one early mission even puts players in the boots of a North Korean soldier hunting a defector. Most players say they finished on Normal in six to eight hours, and anyone who beats it on Realism unlocks YOLO mode , a one-life difficulty that sends you back to the first mission the moment you die.
